newsitem.title: UK: Hyder sees gearing at 100-110 pct until 2000.
newsitem.headline: Hyder sees gearing at 100-110 pct until 2000.

text.p: British multi-utility Hyder Plc expects gearing to remain at 100-110 percent until the year 2000, finance director Paul Twamley told a press conference.
"Gearing is likely to stay around 100-110 percent to 2000," he said.

Gearing is currently 100 percent, up from 95 percent a year ago, the company said in a statement with annual results, which saw pretax profits of 208.2 million pounds, up from 112.9 million previously.
After 2000, gearing "should start to decline," chief executive Graham Hawker said, as the company's capital investment programme is envisaged to "come down somewhat".
But he added that the forecasts could depend on the results of pricing reviews for water and electricity expected in the last two years of the decade.
Hawker said the company felt "comfortable" with gearing at current levels.
Hyder was formed early in 1996 when Welsh Water took over its regional electricity company South Wales Electricity (Swalec). -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
